% Converted, ltx-talk, C-SYMBOL-FONT-TOUNICODE workaround applied: amssymb instead of
% wasysym. $\leadsto$ then extracts as U+21DD and the file passes verapdf -f ua2.
%
% \leadsto is the case to test, not some obviously-wasysym name: BOTH packages define it, so
% a deck that loads both gets the wasy10 glyph with nothing in its source naming wasysym.
% This is how the defect was found on a real course deck.
%
% NOTE THERE IS NO before.tex HERE, deliberately. The usual pattern is that the Beamer
% original holds the property and the naive conversion loses it. That is not this defect:
% the same wasysym $\Box$ under Beamer + pdfTeX ALSO extracts as "2" (measured). The
% corruption is inherited from the deck, not caused by the conversion. What conversion
% changes is the consequence -- the converted deck declares pdfstandard={a-4,ua-2} and so
% now fails clause 8.4.5.8-1 on something it was always doing. There is no "before"
% property to preserve, so asserting one would be a fiction.
\DocumentMetadata{lang=en, pdfversion=2.0, pdfstandard={a-4,ua-2}, tagging=on}
\documentclass{ltx-talk}
\usepackage{amssymb}

\begin{document}
\begin{frame}
\frametitle{Symbol source}
State A $\leadsto$ B done.
\end{frame}
\end{document}
